exclusions_of_note.name: Employers Liability — Contractual Liability Exclusion
exclusions_of_note.impact: Part Two, C.1: EL coverage does not apply to 'liability assumed under a contract' (except warranty of workmanlike manner). If a county contract contains indemnification language requiring Runbeck to assume liability for employee injuries, that contractually assumed liability is NOT covered under Part Two. Only statutory WC benefits (Part One) are unaffected. Significant gap in the context of government contracts with broad indemnification clauses — contractually assumed employer liability is uninsured.

exclusions_of_note.name: Employers Liability — Employment Practices Exclusion
exclusions_of_note.impact: Part Two, C.7: EL excludes damages arising out of coercion, criticism, demotion, evaluation, reassignment, discipline, defamation, harassment, humiliation, discrimination against or termination of any employee, or any personnel practices, policies, acts or omissions. Standard — these claims should be addressed by EPLI. Cross-reference with Management Liability/EPLI policy.

exclusions_of_note.name: Employers Liability — Intentional Injury Exclusion
exclusions_of_note.impact: Part Two, C.5: Excludes 'bodily injury intentionally caused or aggravated by you.' Standard exclusion, but relevant for any operations where supervisory misconduct could be alleged as intentional.

exclusions_of_note.name: Employers Liability — Federal Acts Exclusions (Longshore, FELA, Maritime)
exclusions_of_note.impact: Part Two, C.8-C.10: Excludes Longshore and Harbor Workers, FELA, and maritime crew claims. Not operationally relevant for Runbeck's election services, printing, and mailing operations. Noted for completeness.

exclusions_of_note.name: Employers Liability — Punitive Damages for Illegal Employment
exclusions_of_note.impact: Part Two, C.2-C.3: No coverage for punitive/exemplary damages arising from employing workers in violation of law, nor for BI to employees knowingly employed in violation of law. Standard exclusion.

exclusions_of_note.name: Indiana — Voluntary Compensation Coverage and Other States Insurance Deleted
exclusions_of_note.impact: Section II Voluntary Compensation and EL Coverage (from WC 99 03 01 B) deleted in its entirety for Indiana. Also deletes 60-day Other States notification provision for IN. Employees in Indiana not subject to mandatory WC law have no voluntary compensation fallback under this policy. Verify whether any IN employees fall outside mandatory WC coverage given Runbeck's 31-state footprint.

exclusions_of_note.name: California — Minors Illegally Employed
exclusions_of_note.impact: No coverage for additional compensation under CA Labor Code §4557 for injury to employees under age 16 who were illegally employed. Statutory penalty exposure falls on the insured.

exclusions_of_note.name: California — Punitive/Exemplary Damages
exclusions_of_note.impact: No coverage for punitive or exemplary damages where such insurance is prohibited by law or contrary to public policy under California law. Standard CA restriction.

exclusions_of_note.name: California EL — Liability Assumed Under Contract
exclusions_of_note.impact: Part Two Exclusion 1 amended for CA: excludes liability assumed under a contract. Standard contractual liability exclusion maintained and reinforced under CA law.

exclusions_of_note.name: California EL — Failure to Secure WC Obligations
exclusions_of_note.impact: No EL coverage for injury to an employee when the insured has failed to secure WC obligations under applicable law, or is deprived of statutory/common law defenses or subject to penalty as a result. Insured must maintain full WC compliance or lose EL protection — coverage forfeiture risk if any lapse in CA WC obligations occurs.

exclusions_of_note.name: California EL — Labor Code §2810.3 (Labor Contracting / Joint Liability)
exclusions_of_note.impact: No EL coverage for liability arising from CA Labor Code §2810.3, which imposes joint and several liability on client employers for labor contractor WC failures. If Runbeck uses staffing or labor contractors for CA election operations, this exclusion creates an uninsured EL gap — CA would hold Runbeck jointly liable for contractor WC failures but the policy would not respond.

exclusions_of_note.name: California EL — Flying Crew of Aircraft
exclusions_of_note.impact: No EL coverage for bodily injury to any member of the flying crew of any aircraft. Low relevance for Runbeck's election services/printing/mailing operations.

exclusions_of_note.name: Florida Employers Liability — Intentional Injury Exclusion (FL-Specific Modification)
exclusions_of_note.impact: Replaces standard Exclusion 5, Section C, Part Two for FL only. Excludes coverage for bodily injury intentionally caused or aggravated by the insured, or conduct equivalent to an intentional tort that would otherwise immunize the employer from civil liability under FL WC law. Standard WC statutory benefits (Part One) unaffected; only Employers Liability (Part Two) is modified for FL operations.

exclusions_of_note.name: Trade or Economic Sanctions
exclusions_of_note.impact: No coverage — including claim payment — where prohibited by trade or economic sanctions or other laws or regulations. Broad in scope; applies to entire policy. No material impact for this client absent sanctions exposure.

exclusions_of_note.name: Illinois Contractual Liability and Contribution Waiver Exclusion
exclusions_of_note.impact: For IL operations only: Part Two (EL) excludes liability assumed under contract AND any agreement to waive the right to contribution under the Workers Compensation Act and Workers Occupational Disease Act. Exception preserves warranty of workmanlike manner. Limits ability to contractually assume EL obligations or waive contribution rights under IL law — relevant if any IL county contracts require broad indemnification or contribution waivers.

exclusions_of_note.name: Minnesota Trade Sanctions Exclusion
exclusions_of_note.impact: Coverage does not apply where trade or economic sanctions or other laws/regulations prohibit carrier from providing insurance. MN-specific version of WC 99 06 12. No material impact absent sanctions exposure.

exclusions_of_note.name: Oregon — Intentional Acts / Tortious Conduct (ORS 656.156 / ORS 656.018(3))
exclusions_of_note.impact: Replaces standard Part Two exclusion 5 for OR. Bars EL coverage for bodily injury intentionally caused or aggravated by the insured, or resulting from conduct equivalent to an intentional tort as defined under Oregon statutes, where such conduct causes the insured to lose workers' compensation immunity. OR-specific statutory language replaces the NCCI standard exclusion.

exclusions_of_note.name: Oregon — OSHA/Safety Violations Civil Enforcement (ORS 656.019 / ORS 654.305-654.336)
exclusions_of_note.impact: New exclusion 13 added to Part Two for OR. Bars EL coverage for any cause of action or remedy arising under ORS 656.019 (civil liability for WC fraud) or ORS 654.305-654.336 (Oregon Safe Employment Act — OSHA-equivalent civil enforcement). If OR employees or state regulators pursue civil claims under OR safety statutes, Part Two will not respond — a meaningful gap for OR operations involving election equipment deployment.

wc_specific.experience_mod_note: 0.690 applies to most states (31% below unity). NY: 0.970. AR: 0.660.
wc_specific.monopolistic_states_note: ND, OH, WA, WY correctly excluded from Part One. Stop Gap/EL coverage for all four monopolistic states provided via WC 99 03 01 B Section II-G and CA equivalent WC 99 03 04.
wc_specific.part_three_note: All states except ND, OH, WA, WY covered under Part Three — provides stop-gap for incidental exposures in unlisted states.
wc_specific.waiver_of_subrogation_gap_note: GA, NC, and IL have confirmed WC exposure (premium discount endorsements pp.118, 124, 127) but are NOT listed in blanket WOS endorsement (WC 00 03 13, p.113). If county/government contracts in those states require WOS, a gap exists requiring endorsement amendment.
cancellation_notice_entities: El Paso County Contracts & Procurement Division (Colorado Springs, CO)
wc_specific.unintentional_disclosure_note: WC 99 03 01 B Section III — carrier cannot void coverage for unintentional non-disclosure at inception.
wc_specific.illinois_deductible_note: No per-claim deductible elected for IL claims (WC34-IL, p.129).
wc_specific.indiana_voluntary_comp_note: Voluntary Compensation coverage deleted for IN by WC 99 03 08 (p.111). Verify whether any IN employees are outside mandatory WC coverage.
wc_specific.police_officers_note: Code 7720 (Police Officers) in AZ on $182,294 payroll — likely election site security personnel. Verify job duties match classification; if not actual law enforcement officers, reclassification may be warranted.
wc_specific.freight_handling_note: Code 7360 (Freight Handling Explosives or Ammunition Under Contract: State Act Only) in AZ on $335,329 payroll at $2.56/$100 — highest-rate class on policy. 'Ammunition' is standard NCCI phraseology; likely covers secure ballot transport/chain-of-custody couriers. Verify actual operations with carrier.
wc_specific.voluntary_compensation_note: Voluntary Comp provided for most states via 331-0302 11 17 and WC 99 03 01 B, except Indiana (deleted by WC 99 03 08) and TX (opt-out state).

flags_for_audit.finding: Waiver of Subrogation Gap — GA, NC, IL
flags_for_audit.detail: Blanket WOS endorsement (WC 00 03 13, p.113) covers AZ, AR, CO, FL, IN, MN, NY, OR, PA — but NOT GA, NC, or IL. Premium discount endorsements confirm active WC exposure in all three states (GA p.124, IL p.118, NC p.127). If any county or government contracts in GA, NC, or IL require WOS on the WC policy, the blanket endorsement does not respond. Endorsement amendment needed for those states.

flags_for_audit.finding: California EL — Labor Code §2810.3 Labor Contracting Exclusion
flags_for_audit.detail: WC 04 03 60 B (p.147) excludes EL coverage for liability arising from CA Labor Code §2810.3, which imposes joint and several liability on client employers for labor contractor WC failures. If Runbeck uses staffing or labor contractors for CA election operations (ballot processing, equipment deployment), this creates an uninsured EL exposure. Verify whether any CA operations involve contracted labor.

flags_for_audit.finding: Ownership Change Reporting Requirement — PE-Backed Company
flags_for_audit.detail: WC 00 04 14 A (p.136) requires reporting of any ownership change within 90 days. Failure to report may result in revision of the experience modification factor — which at 0.690 represents significant premium savings. Given Runbeck's PE-backed status, any future ownership transaction (recapitalization, partial exit, full exit, merger) must be reported to carrier within 90 days.

WC 99 03 08 (p.111) deletes Voluntary Compensation coverage for Indiana. Employees in IN not subject to mandatory WC law (e.g., certain sole proprietors, partners, or excluded employees) have no voluntary compensation fallback under this policy. Verify whether any IN-based employees fall outside mandatory WC coverage given Runbeck's 31-state footprint.

flags_for_audit.finding: Code 7360 — Freight Handling Explosives or Ammunition (AZ)
flags_for_audit.detail: Code 7360 (Freight Handling Explosives or Ammunition Under Contract: State Act Only) in AZ with $335,329 payroll at $2.56/$100 — highest-rate classification on the policy. 'Ammunition' phraseology is the NCCI standard description for this code; in context of Runbeck's operations, this likely covers secure ballot transport/chain-of-custody courier operations. 'State Act Only' limitation is appropriate. Verify actual duties with carrier. If misclassified, reclassification could produce meaningful premium savings.

Code 7720 (Police Officers) in AZ on $182,294 payroll. Likely covers security personnel deployed at election sites. Verify that employees classified under this code hold law enforcement credentials or perform duties consistent with this classification. If these are private security contractors without actual law enforcement authority, reclassification may be warranted.

EMR of 0.690 is 31% below unity — reflects strong safety performance. NY uses 0.970 (near unity) under NY independent bureau. Favorable mod generates approximately $13,885 credit in AZ alone. Strong selling point and evidence of a well-managed safety program.

WC 36 06 04 (p.189) adds exclusion 13 barring EL coverage for claims under Oregon Safe Employment Act (ORS 654.305-654.336) civil enforcement. If OR employees or the OR OSHA agency pursues civil remedies for safety violations, Part Two does not respond. Standard OR state filing, but worth noting for operations involving election equipment deployment and personnel management in OR.

flags_for_audit.finding: NY Construction Premium Adjustment Endorsement — Verify Applicability
flags_for_audit.detail: WC 31 03 19 N (p.181) — New York Construction Classification Premium Adjustment Program endorsement is present. Runbeck is not a construction company. Verify why this endorsement is included and whether any eligible NY classification codes apply. If not applicable, no action needed; if applicable, potential premium credit may be available.
